info.name: Referee - Match API
info.description: APIs used by authenticated referees for assigned tournament/match operations. Three separate tournament OTP phases: Toss (existing PUT /toss with otp on initial action), Match Start (/session/start), Match End (/session/end). Independent bookings do not use OTP.

request.description:
Lists only STATUS_ACCEPTED (2) matches. STATUS_ASSIGNED (1) matches are not officiatable and only appear in /match-requests.
Match cards include nullable current_batter/current_bowler from existing roster/runtime resolution, result_margin (null when unproven), booked_by_type and authoritative duration. Never replace null distance/fee/player/result fields with fabricated values.

Includes assignment.status, can_officiate, blocking_code, blocking_reason.
Match cards include nullable current_batter/current_bowler from existing roster/runtime resolution, result_margin (null when unproven), booked_by_type and authoritative duration. Never replace null distance/fee/player/result fields with fabricated values.

Always call GET Toss first to check `data.toss.state`. The state drives which UPDATE action is permitted next.

Roster: `data.teams[].members[]` returns `user_id`, `name`, `mobile_number`, `country_code`, `profile_image_url`, `is_captain`. Roster players expose `user_id` (authoritative id for all scoring/toss payloads), `name` (display label, never a phone number; fallback: profile full name -> team-player name -> users.name -> `Player #{user_id}`), and separate `mobile_number` / `country_code` (nullable, display only; returned only to the assigned referee).

request.description:
Roster: `data.teams[].players[]` returns `user_id`, `name`, `mobile_number`, `country_code`; `data.scoring.runtime.current_*` objects carry the same identity. Roster players expose `user_id` (authoritative id for all scoring/toss payloads), `name` (display label, never a phone number; fallback: profile full name -> team-player name -> users.name -> `Player #{user_id}`), and separate `mobile_number` / `country_code` (nullable, display only; returned only to the assigned referee). The same enriched structure is returned by every successful `PUT /score`.
max_wickets is the effective active batting-team limit shared with runtime, respecting a positive configured cap and roster capacity. Null means no active team/configuration yet. Current engine uses six legal balls per over. result.winner_team_name/message/margin are nullable; do not invent a margin. starting_roles may be empty; follow allowed_actions and next_action.

request.description:
Every successful response includes the same enriched roster (`data.teams[].players[]`: `user_id`, `name`, `mobile_number`, `country_code`). Payload ids (`striker_user_id`, `non_striker_user_id`, `bowler_user_id`, `wicket_keeper_user_id`, `player_id`, `dismissed_user_id`) must always be canonical `user_id` values - never names or mobile numbers.

**Permanent ledger (additive, backward compatible).** Every ADD_EVENT is also stored permanently in `tournament_player_score_events` in the same DB transaction as the score. Optional ADD_EVENT fields: `event_uuid` (UUID - retry key; a replay returns 200 with `data.recorded_event.replayed=true` and never scores twice; reuse for a different event = 409; legacy requests without it cannot be de-duplicated), `runs_source` (BAT | BYE | LEG_BYE, only for NO_BALL and RUN_OUT wickets, attributes the additional runs; omitted = recorded as unattributed), `fielder_user_id` (fielding-team player for run-outs/catches). UNDO_LAST accepts `reason` and returns `data.reversed_event` - the exact ledger row is marked reversed (never deleted). UNDO_LAST is only allowed while the match is LIVE. Note: the endpoint is `PUT /score` (not POST /score/actions).

NEW Cricket ADD_EVENT optional boundary_type: FOUR | SIX | NONE. Actual FOUR/SIX requires 4/6 batter runs; completed running 4 with no boundary send NONE. No-ball hit 4: event_code NO_BALL, value 4, runs_source BAT, boundary_type FOUR; total 5 including penalty. Older clients omitting flag retain legacy inferred 4/6. The PUT score event already creates the shared commentary; no separate create-comment request.
max_wickets is the effective active batting-team limit shared with runtime, respecting a positive configured cap and roster capacity. Null means no active team/configuration yet. Current engine uses six legal balls per over. result.winner_team_name/message/margin are nullable; do not invent a margin. starting_roles may be empty; follow allowed_actions and next_action.

request.description:
Cricket scorecard derived from the permanent scoring-event ledger: team totals (from `score_attributes`), per innings batting/bowling cards, extras, fall of wickets and separate `super_overs`. `data_availability.status` is COMPLETE only when the match was scored with the ledger from START and the ledger reconciles with the team totals; legacy matches are PARTIAL/UNAVAILABLE and player figures are never estimated from team totals. Non-Cricket matches return 422.
Supports authorized tournament and standalone Cricket matches. team_totals is always an object. player_of_match is null until an accepted referee awards an active roster player after match completion, via POST /matches/{matchId}/player-of-match. Once awarded it contains user_id, team_id, name, awarded_at and awarded_by_referee_id. result.margin remains null unless finalized regulation scoring state establishes a safe numeric margin.

request.description:
Example requires accepted referee, live match, batter & bowler set. 4 batter runs + 1 no-ball extra = 5 team runs. Same single ledger event immediately appears in scorecard, commentary, graphs and rankings. Optionally pass unique event_uuid for safe retries. For 4 completed runs but no boundary, use boundary_type NONE.

request.description: One-time Cricket award selected by an accepted referee only after the match is COMPLETED. player_user_id must belong to an active accepted player in either match team roster. Safe idempotent retry with the same ID returns 200; different replacement returns 409. Before completion 409, wrong roster 422, unassigned 404, unauthenticated 401. Persisted in match configuration; readable on GET result, scorecard and match card. No automatic award, reset, DB migration or payout side effect.
